conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_OR_QUALIFIED_CHANGE_REQUIRES_CLA: The flag comes from the OFR line 'Revoked by: EO 10822, May 20, 1959 (in part)'. I read EO 10822 in full: sec. 1 amends EO 10575 'as amended or affected by Executive Order No. 10610' (changes to sections of 10575), and sec. 2 provides 'Part II of Executive Order No. 10610 of May 9, 1955, is hereby revoked', adding that any other provision of EO 10610 inconsistent with the amendments of EO 10575 'shall be subject to such amendment'. That is a real but partial earlier ending (Part II, the Defense Department transfers). It leaves Parts I and III of EO 10610 operating until EO 10893 sec. 305(a)(2), so the qualifier limits 10822 only and does not limit the later whole-order supersession.

notice: Producer research decision only. Independent review and owner adoption remain separate.
rationale: I read the complete held EO 10610 (20 FR 3179, May 11, 1955, signed May 9, 1955, Administration of Mutual Security and Related Functions): Part I (secs. 101-104) transfers Foreign Operations Administration functions to the Secretary of State and the Department of State and sets up the International Cooperation Administration; Part II (secs. 201-202) transfers certain chapter 2 military-assistance functions to the Secretary of Defense; Part III (secs. 301-306) holds definitions, the Operations Coordinating Board proviso (sec. 303(b)), saving of prior actions (sec. 305) and effectiveness (sec. 306). It has no own term. I read the held full text of EO 10893 (25 FR 10731, Nov. 8, 1960, signed Nov. 8, 1960, same title): sec. 305(a), 'The following-described orders, and parts of orders, are hereby superseded', lists in item (2) 'Executive Order No. 10610 of May 9, 1955 (20 F.R. 3179).' (items 1 to 5 are whole orders, 10575, 10610, 10625, 10663 and 10742; item 6 is the part of 10822). That names EO 10610 by number, date and Federal Register page and reaches all of it. The two possible limits do not save the order: sec. 301 provides that the International Cooperation Administration 'including the offices transferred to the Department by the provisions of section 102(a) of Executive Order No. 10610' shall continue in State, but that is an arrangement continued by EO 10893's own text, not a survival of EO 10610; and sec. 306 saves determinations, regulations and other actions taken under affected functions, not the order. The OCR of sec. 305's closing line is garbled ('shall not derogate from the provisions of section 301'), and I read it only as that same link to sec. 301. The ACT:EO:10610>EO:10893 record's quoted slice is a sec. 301(2) passage, not sec. 305, so I cite the ACTOR_TEXT record and rely on the sec. 305(a)(2) wording I read in the held file. D6 self-check: earlier partial events are EO 10625 (Aug. 2, 1955), EO 10663 (1956) and EO 10742 (1957), which amend sections, EO 10700 sec. 6 (1957), which supersedes only the proviso of sec. 303(b) as it relates to the Operations Coordinating Board, and EO 10822 sec. 2 (1959), which revokes Part II; none revokes Parts I and III, and all of them are subsumed by sec. 305(a)(2). EO 10893 sec. 305(a)(6) later supersedes 'sections 1 and 2 of Executive Order No. 10822', so the sec. 2 revocation of Part II is itself superseded in the same sentence, but because EO 10610 as a whole is superseded by item (2) there is nothing for that to revive. After the cited end, EO 10973 sec. 605(a) (1961) supersedes EO 10893 except Part II and funds under sec. 643(c), and EO 12163 (1979) revokes EO 10893; neither names EO 10610 nor restores it, and a text search of the held full-run texts finds EO 10610 named only in EO 10625, 10663, 10700, 10742, 10822 and 10893 (the EO 14257 hit is a tariff-schedule number). The OFR note 'Superseded by: EO 10893, November 8, 1960' agrees; the 1989 snapshot row is empty. Provisional NO hypothesis; the effective end (signing Nov. 8, 1960, no later effective date stated) is not otherwise adjudicated.
